subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding — Pangea Systems kickoff, region selection & autoscale policy
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@pangea-systems.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated capacity for Pangea — proposed kickoff + worksheet attached

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call today — excited to get Pangea onto Dedicated capacity. To keep momentum I attached a short capacity worksheet and an initial SOW draft. Can you confirm the following so we can schedule an ops kickoff?

- Preferred primary region (US-West, US-East, EU-West, etc.)
- Expected baseline concurrent sessions during typical peak (est. qps / concurrency)
- Maximum burst multiple you'd like to support (e.g., 2x baseline)
- Any strict latency P99 target we should aim for (ms)
- Primary contacts for network allowlist and procurement (email + phone)

Proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm region and baseline
- Week of Dec 6: ops kickoff + security questionnaire handoff
- Mid-Dec: regional pool provisioning and warm tests

Attachments: pangea_sow_v1.pdf (draft), capacity_worksheet.xlsx

If that looks good, we can lock in Dec 8–10 for the kickoff.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@pangea-systems.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@pangea-systems.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated capacity for Pangea — proposed kickoff + worksheet attached

Monica,

Thanks — confirmed. Quick answers below:
- Primary regions: US-West (primary) and EU-West (secondary) — we need both to serve NA and EU customers with data residency constraints.
- Baseline concurrency: 600 concurrent sessions (steady during business hours, spiky bursts up to 1500).
- Burst multiple: we prefer a 2.5x burst allowance for Black Friday-type events.
- Latency: P99 under 450ms is our target for generation requests.
- Contacts: ops@pangea-systems.com (network), procurement@pangea-systems.com (procurement)

We'll also need your SOC2 evidence and a list of egress IPs for allowlisting. Dec 8 works for a kickoff — please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Alice Wong
Head of Platform
Pangea Systems

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 10:46:00 -0800
Subject: Pangea onboarding — region selection, autoscale & burst policy (ops kickoff prep)

Team,

Looping you in ahead of the Dec 8 kickoff with Pangea (primary: US-West, secondary: EU-West). Key points from the customer: baseline 600 concurrent, spikes to ~1500, wants 2.5x burst allowance, and P99 target ~450ms. They also requested SOC2 evidence and egress IPs for allowlisting.

Proposed Redwood plan for provisioning and SLOs:
- Regional pools: provision a primary US-West pool (min 6 nodes) and EU-West pool (min 3 nodes) for residency.
- Autoscale policy (proposal): min nodes = as above, target utilization = 55% token-infer throughput per-GPU, scale-up threshold = sustained 70% for 30s, scale-down threshold = below 40% for 3m, cool-down = 120s.
- Burst: implement a burst bucket capacity that allows up to 2.5x baseline for short windows; burst costing agreed per contract. Burst fallback: if regional exhaustion, route to compatible lower-cost model variant in same region (or failover to Dedicated in alternate region only with customer's approval).
- Warm pool / pre-warm: maintain a small warm pool in US-West to reduce cold-start latency during expected spikes (sized to absorb first 30s of a ramp).
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for inference sessions; we should discuss cache TTL with customer during kickoff.

Requests for Karthik and Rishi:
1) Karthik — confirm feasibility and lead times for provisioning the proposed pool sizes in US-West and EU-West. Any known capacity constraints for Dec/Jan?
2) Rishi — can you provide recommended quantization profile and model variant to hit P99 ~450ms at 600 concurrency? Also give estimate for token cost delta when using the burst variant.

Attachments: activation_checklist.md (draft) — I'm sharing the checklist we use for ops handover.

I will run the kickoff and collect the allowlist and SOC2 pointer from the customer.

Thanks,
Irene
Customer Success Lead, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pangea onboarding — region selection, autoscale & burst policy (ops kickoff prep)

Irene — reviewing capacity constraints now. Quick notes:
- US-West: we have available quota to turn up 6-node pool in the third week of Dec; lead time ~5 business days to finalize networking and IPs.
- EU-West: smaller pool (3 nodes) is feasible but requires quota ticket — estimate lead time ~7 business days given region provisioning timelines.
- We should pin the instance types (A100/80GB equivalent) for latency predictability; I'll add recommended instance SKU in the runbook.

I've uploaded a short regional plan and estimated GPU-hours to the drive link below. Also attaching a PDF with our suggested pool topology.

Attachments: regional_capacity_plan.pdf
Related: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0B_pangea_activation

I'll coordinate with infra to reserve capacity once we get the signed SOW and allowlist.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@pangea-systems.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Pangea Dedicated onboarding — ops kickoff notes, next steps & mutual action plan

Alice / Pangea team,

Thanks for the kickoff earlier this week. Recap and agreed next steps below:

1) Regions & pools
- US-West (primary): provision 6-node pool (A100-equivalent), warm pool configured for first-30s ramp.
- EU-West (secondary): provision 3-node pool (same SKU), data residency for EU traffic.

2) Autoscale & burst
- Autoscale policy: target util 55%, scale up at sustained 70% for 30s, scale down below 40% for 3m, cooldown 120s.
- Burst: allow up to 2.5x baseline for short windows with burst bucket; cost shown in SOW. If regional capacity is exhausted, we will route to fallback model variant in-region; cross-region failover only on explicit customer opt-in.

3) Network/security items needed from Pangea (action by Dec 24):
- Static egress IP allowlist (ops@pangea-systems.com)
- Point-of-contact for SOC2 evidence review (email)
- Any additional IP ranges for upstream integrations

4) Infra/ops tasks (Redwood)
- Karthik to file quota ticket and reserve US-West pool (ETA: 5 business days after signed SOW).
- Rishi to confirm quantization/model variant and share perf/cost delta (ETA: 3 business days).
- Monica/Irene to coordinate SOW signature and procurement path.

Attachments referenced above: pangea_sow_v1.pdf, capacity_worksheet.xlsx, activation_checklist.md, regional_capacity_plan.pdf

Calendar: I've scheduled the first technical validation window on Jan 4, 2027 (09:00 PT) — invite sent separately.

If that summary looks correct, please confirm the allowlist and SOC2 contact by Dec 24 and we will start provisioning the pools.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Customer Success Lead, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
